newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA'S LITIMPEKS SAYS WORST BEHIND IT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA'S LITIMPEKS SAYS WORST BEHIND IT.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank, one of the two banks whose closure at the end of 1995 started a bank crisis, said on Wednesday that it expected brighter prospects in 1997 after the 1996 problems.
"The year 1996 was a difficult year but the worst is behind us," Litimpeks deputy chairman Jonas Bobelis told Reuters in an interview.
Bobelis declined to say what the 1996 financial results of the bank were before the shareholders' meeting, which is sheduled for March 27.
"1997 will be a good year for Litimpeks," Bobelis added.
Analysts say the bank needs to attract outside investment to compete in the Lithuanian markets.

Bobelis ealier told Reuters that Litimpeks planned to launch a 50 million litas new share issue this year and that it was negotiating with a number of foreign banks and investment funds to sell them a stake in the bank.
He said that Estonian banks Hoiupank and Tallinna Pank were among the banks who had expressed an interest in buying the new Litimpeks shares.
The registered share capital of Litimpeks is currently 41.1 million litas.

Lithuania was hit by a banking crisis in late 1995 when two of the leading country's bank Litimpeks and Innovation were shut down. Litimpeks was reopened in mid-1996 while Innovation Bank is to be liquidated.
"We feel that the government's decisions to shut down the bank for six months and then to reopen it was unjustified," Bobelis said.

The audited financial results of the country's commercial banks for 1996 showed that the sector seems to have recovered well from the crisis but opinion polls show that it is still short of customers' confidence.
